title: Toward Compact Fiber In-line Nonlinear Devices via Highly Efficient Nanophotonic Cavity Interface
authors: Mahsa Haddadi Moghaddam, Kirlie Iulius Figuera Michal, Sangwoo Lee, Sijin Sung, Jongwon Lee, Hyeong-Ryeol Park, Je-Hyung Kim
abstract: Compact and efficient frequency conversion within optical fibers is highly desirable for nonlinear and quantum photonic technologies, yet it remains challenging due to weak nonlinear interactions and limited coupling efficiencies onto optical fibers. Here, we demonstrate resonantly enhanced second-harmonic generation (SHG) through the all-fiber integration of a gallium nitride (GaN) hole-type circular Bragg grating (h-CBG) cavity, directly transferred onto a standard optical fiber. Together with the large second-order nonlinear susceptibility and wide optical transparency window of GaN, the fabricated h-CBG membrane cavity on GaN enables strong field confinement and vertically directional out-coupling of the generated SHG signal. As a result, we observe drastically enhanced SHG signals from the h-CBG device compared with the bulk GaN and the unpatterned freestanding GaN membrane. Using a deterministic pick-and-place transfer technique, we demonstrate robust and precise fiber integration of the GaN cavity device, enabling in-line SHG generation from a conventional fiber platform. This work establishes a compact and scalable approach for incorporating optical nonlinearity into fiber-based photonic systems.
summary: The research presents a method to create compact, high-efficiency nonlinear optical devices by integrating Gallium Nitride (GaN) hole-type circular Bragg grating cavities onto standard optical fibers. By leveraging the cavity's resonant enhancement and directional coupling, they achieved significantly boosted Second-Harmonic Generation signals. This establishes a practical and scalable platform for incorporating strong nonlinearity into fiber-based quantum and classical photonic systems.
main_problem: The challenge is achieving compact and efficient frequency conversion, specifically Second-Harmonic Generation (SHG), within optical fibers for advanced nonlinear and quantum photonic technologies.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a scalable approach by integrating a Gallium Nitride (GaN) hole-type circular Bragg grating (h-CBG) cavity directly onto an optical fiber, achieving drastically enhanced SHG signals.
method: They utilized deterministic pick-and-place transfer techniques to integrate the fabricated GaN h-CBG membrane cavity onto a standard fiber core and characterized performance using pulsed laser spectroscopy.
model_or_system: The physical system is an all-fiber integrated nonlinear device based on a GaN h-CBG structure. This grating acts as a resonant cavity, confining light fields to enhance the second-order nonlinear susceptibility ($\chi^2$) interaction for SHG generation.
key_observables: SHG signal enhancement factor (up to $\sim 32	imes$ vs. freestanding membrane), resonance wavelength ($\approx 784 	ext{ nm}$), and power-normalized conversion efficiency ($3.62 	imes 10^{-3} 	ext{ W}^{-1}$).
important_parameters: GaN material properties, cavity geometry parameters (e.g., radial period $r$, hole size $a$), and pump wavelength ($\approx 784 	ext{ nm}$ for SHG at $\lambda/2$).
main_assumptions: The efficiency calculations rely on estimating peak intensity from average power measurements using the known pulse characteristics of the Ti:Sapphire laser.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device schematic, simulated far-field radiation patterns showing directional out-coupling, measured cavity mode spectra confirming resonance at $784 	ext{ nm}$, and setups detailing both SHG measurement and the deterministic fiber transfer process.
paper_structure: The paper details the fabrication of GaN h-CBG membranes via etching, characterizes the resonant optical properties using spectroscopy, demonstrates the high efficiency of SHG generation within the cavity structure, and concludes with a successful demonstration of robust, in-line integration onto an optical fiber platform.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems because it provides a solid platform for generating strong nonlinear light sources (like entangled photons or frequency-converted light) directly within standard telecom fibers, which is crucial for building quantum communication networks.
